pipeline pipe·line | ˈpīpˌlīn | noun 1 a long pipe, typically underground, for conveying oil, gas, etc. over long distances. • a channel supplying goods or information: the biggest heroin pipeline in history. 2 Computing a linear sequence of specialized modules used for pipelining. 3 Surfing the hollow formed by the breaking of a large wave. verb [with object] 1 convey (a substance) by a pipeline: oil and gas were pipelined to refineries in Toronto. 2 Computing design or execute (a computer or instruction) using the technique of pipelining: chip designers pipeline the instructions given to the hardware. PHRASES in the pipeline awaiting completion or processing; being developed: new treatments are in the pipeline.
